briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-008
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- office roof: (82, 99), roof
- control room: (-132, 2), indoor
- gate 2: (26, 112), outdoor
- antenna mast: (48, -82), outdoor

Robots:
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 23 kg), camera. Endurance: 4620 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 10 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2580 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1140 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Deliver the toolkit (7 kg) to control room. Location: control room. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 7 kg).
- T2: Tighten the valve at antenna mast. Location: antenna mast. Duration: 120 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 480 s.
- T3: Photograph gate 2 for the condition report. Location: gate 2. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera.
- T4: Inspect office roof with a camera. Location: office roof. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera.
- T5: Inspect office roof with a camera. Location: office roof. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 180 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 600 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: office roof (82, 99, a rooftop); control room (-132, 2, indoors); gate 2 (26, 112, outside); antenna mast (48, -82, outside).

The fleet: G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 23 kg at 2.5 m/s and runs for 77 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 10 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 43 minutes including getting back. D1, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera and a thermal camera, cruises at 8 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 19 minutes of flight time, return trip included.

Jobs:
(T1) Get the toolkit (7 kg) over to control room - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T2) Someone has to tighten the valve at antenna mast - that takes 2 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 8 minutes.
(T3) We need pictures of gate 2 for the report - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T4) Have a look at office roof - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T5) Do a visual check of office roof - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 3 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 10 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
